thread:
Alex Chen: Heads up — compliance pinged about extending security log retention and locking down SIEM exports. We need a short decision by EOD. Current sketch: Kinesis Firehose -> s3://redwood-audit-prod -> SIEM. Who has read access? KMS key? RBAC?
Maya Patel: High level Q: which log classes are we talking about? App access logs vs privileged audit logs vs billing events? Compliance might only care about privileged/auth/audit events.
Jordan (sec-eng): Legal flagged financial/audit events need up to 7 years. Auth/audit should default to 7y unless we get explicit waiver. App debug logs can be 90-180d.
Samir Rao: Implementation note — Firehose can deliver to a dedicated audit bucket in the security account. We should put lifecycle rules: hot 30d (S3 Standard), transition to Glacier Deep Archive, expire after 7 years. Cross-account Firehose needs write permissions and KMS decrypt permissions on the CMK.
Alex Chen: Important: developers must not have ad-hoc read access to that bucket. Only security+compliance roles should be able to access.
Maya Patel: Agreed. RBAC plan: create roles "sec-audit-reader" and "sec-compliance-analyst". No dev groups. Add periodic access review.
Samir Rao: Example Firehose IAM trust + bucket policy we can use (snip):
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect": "Allow", "Principal": {"Service": "firehose.amazonaws.com"}, "Action": "s3:PutObject", "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::redwood-audit-prod/*"},
    {"Effect": "Deny", "Principal": "*", "Action": "s3:ListBucket", "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::redwood-audit-prod", "Condition": {"StringNotEquals": {"aws:PrincipalTag/role": "sec-audit-reader"}}}
  ]
}
```
Samir Rao: KMS recommendation: use a customer-managed CMK in the security account with alias "alias/sec/audit-cmk". Key policy should allow Firehose service principal to encrypt/envelope-decrypt and only allow principals in the security account to create grants. Rotation enabled.
Jordan (sec-eng): Quick key policy sketch for review:
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {"Sid": "Allow use by firehose", "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": {"Service": "firehose.amazonaws.com"}, "Action": ["kms:Encrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"], "Resource": "*"},
    {"Sid": "Allow security account admins", "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/sec-admin"}, "Action": "kms:*", "Resource": "*"}
  ]
}
```
Maya Patel: Also: audit logs should be immutable where possible. Enable S3 Object Lock (governance mode) for the audit prefix for the 7y retention.
Alex Chen: Good call. That prevents accidental deletions by misconfigured roles.
security-bot: Ticket created: SEC-4821 — "Audit bucket retention & SIEM export access" (assigned to Samir Rao).
ops-oncall: I can run a staged export to staging bucket tomorrow morning and verify KMS decrypt for the SIEM sidecar. Please create a test principal for the SIEM integration.
Samir Rao: Action plan I can implement today: 1) Create s3://redwood-audit-prod in security acct 2) Configure Firehose with IAM role and CMK alias/sec/audit-cmk 3) Put lifecycle + object-lock + bucket policy 4) Add CloudTrail event selector so bucket writes are logged to a separate audit trail.
Maya Patel: Security will: 1) Create sec-audit-reader & sec-compliance-analyst roles 2) Add IAM permission boundary to block s3:* and kms:* unless explicitly allowed 3) Schedule quarterly access review 4) Draft SOP for request flow.
Jordan (sec-eng): Compliance will confirm whether full 7-year retention applies to all audit prefixes or just financial/auth events. For now we treat "audit/privileged/*" as 7y.
Alex Chen: Decision for implementation:
- Hot window: 30 days (S3 Standard)
- Transition to Glacier Deep Archive after 30d
- Retain immutable copy for 7 years using Object Lock (governance)
- SIEM export via Kinesis Firehose -> s3://redwood-audit-prod (security acct)
- Encryption: CMK alias/sec/audit-cmk in security account, rotation enabled
- RBAC: only sec-audit-reader and sec-compliance-analyst roles have list/get permissions; no dev-access.
- Audit: CloudTrail logs for bucket events + Key usage logs to separate monitoring account.

Samir Rao: Quick CLI examples for the runbook:
```bash
# create key
aws kms create-key --description "Audit CMK (security acct)" --tags TagKey=owner,TagValue=security
aws kms create-alias --alias-name alias/sec/audit-cmk --target-key-id <key-id>

# lifecycle (JSON file) apply
aws s3api put-bucket-lifecycle-configuration --bucket redwood-audit-prod --lifecycle-configuration file://lifecycle.json
```
```json
# lifecycle.json (snippet)
{
  "Rules": [
    {"ID": "hot-to-glacier", "Status": "Enabled", "Filter": {"Prefix": "audit/"}, "Transitions": [{"Days": 30, "StorageClass": "DEEP_ARCHIVE"}], "Expiration": {"Days": 2555}} 
  ]
}
```
Maya Patel: Follow-ups: Jordan, can you confirm with legal about whether billing/usage events need the same retention? If not, we keep them at 1 year.
Jordan (sec-eng): Will do, pinging legal now.
Alex Chen: Good. Assignments: Samir (create infra + run staging test) | Maya (roles + SOP) | Jordan (legal confirmation) | Alex (monitor SEC-4821 and approve PR).
security-bot: SEC-4821 updated: Samir moved to In Progress.
Samir Rao: I'll post the PR for bucket policy and CMK key policy once the staging test passes. ETA: tomorrow EOD.
Alex Chen: Thanks all — let's aim to have prod changes in the following maintenance window next week. :thumbsup:
ops-oncall: Aye. I'll block the window and add a rollback playbook for accidental key issues.
Maya Patel: Adding a note: we should also add a short eval to Redwood Optimize to flag any sudden spike in export volume (possible exfil).
Jordan (sec-eng): Nice. Closing note: no ad-hoc console access for devs — requests must go through sec change control and be logged in SEC-4821.
Alex Chen: Closing thread.
